record.summary: Guidelines by the High-Level Expert Group on AI set up by the European Commission on what makes AI trustworthy: lawful, respecting all applicable laws; ethical, respecting ethical principles and values; and robust, technically and with regard to its social environment. They set seven key requirements: human agency and oversight; technical robustness and safety, including a fall back plan; privacy and data governance; transparency, including that people know they are interacting with an AI system; diversity, non-discrimination and fairness; societal and environmental well-being; and accountability, with auditability and redress. An assessment list helps verify that they are met.
record.notes: Written by the High-Level Expert Group on Artificial Intelligence (AI HLEG), an independent expert group that the European Commission set up in June 2018, and presented on 8 April 2019, after a first draft published in December 2018 drew more than 500 comments in an open consultation. The assessment list in the guidelines was piloted by the Commission from 26 June to 1 December 2019; on that basis the AI HLEG presented the final Assessment List for Trustworthy AI (ALTAI), a self-assessment checklist and the group's third deliverable, in July 2020 (made public on 17 July 2020). The guidelines are offered in 23 EU languages, together with a separate AI HLEG document on the definition of AI used for their purpose.

verification.note: Stored and read: the Commission's library page for the guidelines on digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu (HTML and printable PDF, last updated 31 January 2024), which gives the title, presentation by the AI HLEG on 8 April 2019, the first draft of December 2018, the three components and seven key requirements, the piloting and ALTAI, and downloads in 23 languages; and the AI HLEG's ALTAI (July 2020), which says the group was set up by the Commission in June 2018, dates the guidelines to 8 April 2019 and the piloting to 26 June to 1 December 2019. The guidelines' own English text is not among this record's stored files, so claims that rest on it alone were removed. No stored source says the guidelines were withdrawn or replaced. The document carries no document number, so official_identifier is empty.

legal_force.quote: The Guidelines put forward a set of 7 key requirements that AI systems should meet in order to be deemed trustworthy.
This Assessment List for Trustworthy AI (ALTAI) is intended for self-evaluation purposes.

summary.quote: (1) lawful - respecting all applicable laws and regulations
(2) ethical - respecting ethical principles and values
(3) robust - both from a technical perspective while taking into account its social environment
A specific assessment list aims to help verify the application of each of the key requirements:
Human agency and oversight: AI systems should empower human beings, allowing them to make informed decisions and fostering their fundamental rights.
They need to be safe, ensuring a fall back plan in case something goes wrong, as well as being accurate, reliable and reproducible.
Humans need to be aware that they are interacting with an AI system, and must be informed of the system’s capabilities and limitations.

Auditability, which enables the assessment of algorithms, data and design processes plays a key role therein, especially in critical applications. Moreover, adequate an accessible redress should be ensured.
5. Diversity, Non-discrimination and Fairness; 6. Societal and Environmental Well-being; 7. Accountability.

judgment.status_reasoning: Presented on 8 April 2019. The Commission's library page, last updated on 31 January 2024, still offers the guidelines for download in 23 languages, and no stored source says they were withdrawn or replaced; ALTAI (2020) builds on them rather than replacing them. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: Precedent in pipeline/scope-decisions.md: a report an authority publishes that an expert group it convened wrote is in, with a scope_note naming the group and the authority as issuing body; the existing scope_note does that.

open_questions: The guidelines' own English text is not among this record's stored files: its download link on the Commission's library page (ec.europa.eu/newsroom/dae/document.cfm?doc_id=60419) is under a robots.txt Disallow (/newsroom/dae/), and no other official copy that can be stored was found (the Publications Office record d3988569-0434-11ea-8c1f-01aa75ed71a1 offers the PDF only through a script). A maintainer could provide the PDF with tools/archive.py --provide and propose it as secondary_url.

Removed until the guidelines' text is stored: the four ethical principles (respect for human autonomy, prevention of harm, fairness, explicability), the critical concerns (identification of individuals, covert AI systems, citizen scoring, lethal autonomous weapons), the AI HLEG's 52 members and its two mandated deliverables, the disclaimer that the guidelines are not an official Commission position, the date 18 December 2018 for the first draft, and a fundamental rights impact assessment before development.
